title: A Book Review - Ranji the Music Maker

topics.name: A few / a little (countable and uncountable)

questions.rule: The adjective comes before the noun, and old starts with a vowel sound: an old flute.

options: The crow sang better than Ranji.
The crow sang more better than Ranji.
The crow sang good than Ranji.
questions.rule: Better is already the comparative of good/well. Never say more better.
Notes can be counted, so use a few with a plural noun: a few notes.

questions.rule: Comparing two things with than needs the comparative: smaller than.

Article + adjective + noun: an old flute.
Comparative + than compares two things: smaller than.

chat: Ranji
Do you have any milk for the kitten?
options: Yes, I have a little milk.
Yes, I have a few milk.
questions.rule: Milk is uncountable, so use a little, not a few or many.

options: Ranji walked slow down the lane.

Ranji walked slowly down the lane.
questions.rule: An adverb of manner describes the verb: walked slowly. The story is in the past: walked.

options: This is the beautifulest song I know.

questions.rule: Long adjectives form the superlative with the most: the most beautiful.

The adverb comes after the verb: listened very closely.

chat: Asha
Which is bigger, a cat or a tiger?
options: A tiger is much bigger than a cat.
A tiger is much big than a cat.
A tiger is much more bigger than a cat.
questions.rule: Short adjectives add -er: bigger than. Don't add more as well.

chat: Coach
How did your team play today?
options: We played really good and won!
We played really well and win!
We played really well and won!
questions.rule: Well is the adverb of good: played well. Keep the past tense: won.
Adjectives never take a plural -s and come before the noun: green eyes.

options: Few people liked Ranji's music, but the cats loved it.
Few people likes Ranji's music, but the cats loved it.
A little people liked Ranji's music, but the cats loved it.
questions.rule: People is countable, so use few, and the verb stays in the past: liked.

options: Ranji's drum was as louder as thunder.

Ranji's drum was as loud than thunder.
questions.rule: For equal things use as + plain adjective + as: as loud as.

questions.rule: Cats can be counted, so use a few, not a little.

questions.rule: Good is irregular: good, better, best. Here we compare before and after.
Before the noun sound we need an adjective: a strange sound.

chat: Mum

options: Only a few. Most of them have gone home.
Only a little. Most of them have gone home.
Only a few. Most of them has gone home.
questions.rule: How many asks about countable things, so answer with a few. Most of them takes have.

questions.rule: Bananas can be counted (a few); rice cannot (a little).
Comparing one with the whole group uses the superlative: the best.
Size comes before colour: a large black cat, not a black large cat.

chat: Meera

chat: Shopkeeper

options: Just a few, please. Half a kilo is enough.
Just a little, please. Half a kilo are enough.
Just a little, please. Half a kilo is enough.
questions.rule: Sugar is uncountable: a little. One amount (half a kilo) takes is.

options: Of all the children, Ranji played the most loud.
Of all the children, Ranji played the more loudly.
Of all the children, Ranji played the most loudly.
questions.rule: Comparing with a whole group needs the superlative of the adverb: the most loudly.

options: Ranji had a few friend, so he was often lonely.
Ranji had few friends, so he were often lonely.
Ranji had few friends, so he was often lonely.
questions.rule: Few (without a) means almost none and takes a plural noun; he takes was.

questions.rule: Noise is uncountable; little (without a) means almost none.
The more ..., the + comparative: the more he practised, the better he played.
A few goes before a plural countable noun: a few cats.

chat: Grandpa
Did Ranji play the flute well?
options: At first he played badly, but soon his notes sounded sweet.
At first he played bad, but soon his notes sounded sweet.
At first he played badly, but soon his notes sounded sweetly.
questions.rule: Action verb + adverb: played badly. Sounded describing notes + adjective: sweet.

chat: Anu
Which book did you like the most this year?
options: 'Ranji the Music Maker' was the most funniest book I read this year.
'Ranji the Music Maker' was the funniest book I read this year.
'Ranji the Music Maker' was the funnier book I read this year.
questions.rule: One out of many books: superlative the funniest. Never most funniest.

chat: Teacher
Did many students bring books for the book fair?
options: Not much. Only a few students brought books.
Not many. Only a little students brought books.
Not many. Only a few students brought books.
questions.rule: Students are countable: not many, a few students.
